items.title: 66096_Monk Montgomery oral history interview
items.q: There were changes come along a little later, like Clifford Brown, Benny Bailey.

ctx.x: ...So I turned it down on my control back here. I always made sure when I went on the stand that I had my gain up high, because I knew that Hamp was going to turn his up and I'd turn mine back. As soon as he'd kind of walk out of my range, I'd turn it back down to what I thought was a good balance for the band, you see.

But back to what the musicians in the band...and he had quite a few good, top people in the band during the period I was there. Just to name some of the personnel: in the trumpet section it was Art Farmer, there was Quincy Jones, there was Al Williams, there was The Whistler. There were changes come along a little later, like Clifford Brown, Benny Bailey. And also Emory -- gosh, I can't think of Emory's -- big, fat trumpet player. I can't think of his name, but we used to call him the Fat Boy because he was huge,…

The trombone section was Jimmy Cleveland, Buster Cooper and Al -- oh, I'm sorry, I can't think of that trombone player's name (Hayes). And the rhythm section -- the reed section was Bobby Plater, he was beautiful, Bobby Plater; Morris Lane, Clifford Solomon, Oscar Estelle, the baritone, and...who else am I missing? It's been a lot of years and I keep...I've got up to the date in my mind.
